02

The problem

AI learns once (at tremendous cost), then is frozen.

Training one model used enough electricity to power 2,000 US homes for a year. Then it shipped, and it never learned again.

21.6 GWh

to learn once · each square is one US home for a year

0

lessons after it ships

Meta Llama 3.1 405B model card: 30.84M GPU-hours × 700 W ≈ 21.6 GWh. Average US home: 10,791 kWh a year (EIA, 2022).

03

We think this is the most important problem in AI.

Meet the Experience Model.

A new kind of model, built from how the brain computes, that learns continuously with a fraction of the parameters and memory.

  • Small enough to run anywhere.
  • Light enough to learn forever.

06

Evidence

It learns live, in real time. From 61.8% to 100% on a voice it had never heard.

No retraining. It learned the new voice while running, and forgot less on other speakers than backprop: 6.43 vs. 11.07 points.

Telepath speaker-adaptation study (2026). Start and end accuracy measured; the path between them is illustrative.

07

Memory

Learns with 1/16,000 of the memory.

Backprop through time stores every step it sees. Telepath stores one, at any length.

Telepath: 1 step

Backprop: 16,000 steps, and growing

Learning state at a 16,000-step sequence, an internal estimate. Not total RAM, energy or system cost.

Appendix

The evidence

If every parameter were a sheet of paper.

The 369M-parameter model would stack 36.9 km high, four times higher than Everest. Telepath would stand 11 meters, about a three-story building. On abnormal brain activity, they score the same.

One sheet of office paper ≈ 0.1 mm. LaBraM-Huge: 369M parameters, 0.826 AUROC on TUAB abnormal EEG. Telepath: 110k parameters, 0.827. SAMBA: 1.0M.

A1

NeurIPS 2026 · Spotlight

Teaching slow networks to look ahead.

Shivang Rawat, Mirko Morello, Flaviano Morone, David J. Heeger

Brain-like layers integrate over time, so deep stacks fall behind their inputs. Recursive Quadrature Filters plus a parameter-free look-ahead let each layer respond to where its input is going, not where it was.

96.1%

spoken words from the raw waveform, with a 31.9k-parameter model

83.6%

Path-X, 16,384 steps, with a minimal forward-only model

+15.2

points from look-ahead in a six-layer network

Prospective Coding Improves Learning in Deep Continuous-Time Recurrent Networks. NeurIPS 2026, spotlight paper. Five seeds per comparison.

A2

NeurIPS 2026 Workshop · Foundation Models for the Brain and Body

A tiny brain-signal model that learns by guessing what comes next.

Mirko Morello, Shivang Rawat, David J. Heeger

An encoder made of tuned oscillators learns from unlabeled brain recordings by forecasting them. At 110,000 parameters it rivals models thirty to three thousand times its size.

0.925

abnormal-EEG AUROC with 110k parameters; SAMBA reaches 0.905 with 1.0M

0.882

speech onset in intracranial recordings, 2.9 points above the best published

0.822

sleep-staging balanced accuracy, above a model 308× larger

Self-Supervised Learning with Recursive Quadrature Filters for Neural Time Series. Patient-disjoint or chronological splits; test set touched once.

A3

PNAS · 2019

Memory that you can move.

David J. Heeger, Wayne Mackey

ORGaNICs: a brain-inspired circuit that holds a memory without any input, updates it as the world shifts, and stays stable while it does both. It is the lineage behind the Recursive Quadrature Filter.

Holds

a memory with no input, like working memory in cortex

Moves

updates the memory as the world shifts

Stays stable

while doing both: the foundation for RQFs

Oscillatory recurrent gated neural integrator circuits (ORGaNICs), a unifying theoretical framework for neural dynamics. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 2019.

A5

95% accurate sounds good. Until you use it all day.

~800

mistakes a day, at 5% error, for a person who speaks about 16,000 words a day.

One request, 42 words, at 5% error

Can you move my three o’clock with Dana Donna to Thursday and send her the notes from the board meeting? Also remind me to call Dad on the way home, and add oat oak milk, eggs and coffee to the grocery list before Sunday.

Words per day: Mehl et al., Science (2007). Error counts are arithmetic: 16,000 × 5%. Example transcript is illustrative.

A10

The same problem, one level deeper: thought.

State of the art today

97.5%

word accuracy for a man with ALS speaking through an implanted BCI, 125,000-word vocabulary.

UC Davis, NEJM (2024).

Why it isn’t solved

Brain signals drift from hour to hour and day to day. Frozen decoders slip, and need recalibration sessions to recover.

Telepath

1st

on detecting speech in the brain, with a model ~1,700× smaller. Built to keep learning as the signal drifts.

Telepath benchmark results.

A12

What zero error makes possible.

Her voice, back

A woman with ALS speaks to her kids through a BCI that never mishears her, and understands her better every week.

His words, after a stroke

An assistant that learns a stroke survivor’s changed speech in days, not the months a new model would take.

Every child understood

A reading tutor that understands a four-year-old’s speech, lisp and all, and grows up alongside them.

Every word in the room

Clinical notes, cockpits, factory floors: places where a single wrong word matters, and the speaker never changes.

Product visions, not current products.

What this round funds

From proof to product.

1

Phase 1

Prove it at scale

Scale local learning on the speech model, and reach 100% accuracy on new speech, learned live.

Put it on devices

Live learning on phone- and edge-class hardware, and a local-learning decision model.

Cambium: continuous learning on top of frozen open-source models, with first design partners.

Each phase de-risks the next.
